summary: The article accurately highlights the liquidity risks in small-cap funds, citing relevant SEBI regulations and recent stress test data. The claims about liquidation times and regulatory requirements are largely consistent with authoritative sources.

claims.claim: SEBI data indicates that top small-cap funds can take significantly longer to liquidate half their portfolios compared to mid-cap funds.
claims.note: SEBI's FY26 annual report shows small-cap funds could take longer than mid-cap funds to liquidate half their portfolios.

claims.claim: Small-cap funds required an average of 51 days to sell half their assets, while mid-cap funds needed only 23 days as per FY26 data.
claims.note: During March 2026, among the top five schemes, the average liquidation time was 51 days for small-cap funds, compared with 23 days for mid-cap funds, as per SEBI's FY26 stress-test data.

claims.claim: SEBI, as the market regulator, mandates mutual fund houses to conduct stress tests on their small-cap and mid-cap schemes.
claims.note: AMFI publishes stress test results for midcap and smallcap mutual fund schemes as directed by SEBI.

claims.claim: Fund managers might even have to gate redemptions (i.e., temporarily stop or limit withdrawals) or stagger payouts over several days, weeks, or even months, as permitted by SEBI regulations under extreme circumstances.
claims.note: SEBI circulars from 2016 and later provide details on circumstances where mutual funds can impose restrictions on redemptions, not exceeding ten working days in any 90-day period, and typically for requests above ₹2 lakh.

claims.claim: Reviewing the stress test reports published by Asset Management Companies (AMCs) on the AMFI India website can provide valuable insights into a fund's liquidity profile.
claims.note: AMFI India's website is the official portal where stress test reports for mutual funds are published.

claims.claim: SEBI notified the Mutual Funds Regulations, 2026 on 14 January 2026, replacing the 1996 framework that had governed India's mutual fund industry for nearly three decades. The new rules took effect on 1 April 2026.
claims.note: SEBI notified the Mutual Funds Regulations, 2026 on January 14, 2026, which became effective from April 1, 2026, replacing the 1996 framework.

article_title: Small-Cap Funds: Understanding Liquidity Risk and Longer Redemption Times
